questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right side can encourage the passing driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned when riding in a group?

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the newer riders at the same time.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do with your head and shoulders?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to improve your view.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal as soon as you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving your signal on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What does the Motorcycle Safety Foundation's SEE strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When can you ride a motorized bicycle or moped in a bicycle lane?

options.text: Never. Motorized bicycles may never be used in bicycle lanes.
Only when carrying a passenger.
Only when authorized by local ordinance or law enforcement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when authorized by local ordinance or law enforcement.
questions.explanation: Motorized bicycles and mopeds can only be used in bicycle lanes if local laws or law enforcement allow it.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles will protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
A windshield will protect you from the wind, but goggles won't.
A windshield will keep your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles will protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle to see oncoming traffic and be visible to others. On a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane to see ahead. On a right curve, ride on the left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling below 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and keep the motorcycle going straight. Only brake after you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road safely.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They provide a more narrow view of the road.
They provide a wider view of the road.
They provide a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make vehicles behind you look farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Instead, use only the rear brake to slow down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light warns that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle operators?

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators must wear proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: If you will be carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure adjustments.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You will need to increase tire pressure a few pounds before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct tire pressure.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid car doors opening, people stepping into the lane, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change your position as needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Always complete passes within the posted speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, you should NOT:

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed accordingly.
Make your presence known by sounding your horn and/or using lights or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always communicate with other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Also adjust your speed to match the situation and change your lane position or direction if needed.

questions.question: If you wear a protective jacket while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: A sturdy riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, jackets also help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: A "wobble" is when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly shake. This is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improperly tightening the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: A motorcyclist may NOT place a toll road transponder:

options.text: On the windshield of their motorcycle.
In their pocket.
Under their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under their seat.
questions.explanation: A transponder can be placed in your pocket, in a cycle net on the gas tank, on a license plate holder, in a storage compartment, or on the windshield. The toll reader must be able to detect it.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, ride carefully. Keep your hand near the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the part of the lane that will make you visible to other drivers as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the part of the lane that will make you visible to other drivers as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of the lane that will make you visible to other drivers as soon as possible at a blind intersection.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you are going. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders may cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther away.
Is not recommended because it may make the other driver move back too early.
Has no impact on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may make the other driver move back too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may prompt the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because you cannot get used to any part of a lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other motorists.
A good idea when road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good idea when road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions require.
